plain.text: Once safely on shore, they found the island was Malta. The islanders showed unusual kindness and built a fire because it was raining and cold. As Paul gathered sticks, a viper fastened itself on his hand. The islanders said, "This man must be a murderer; though he escaped the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live." But Paul shook the snake off into the fire and suffered no ill effects. When nothing happened, they changed their minds and said he was a god. Publius, the chief official of the island, welcomed them. His father was sick in bed with fever and dysentery. Paul prayed, placed his hands on him and healed him. Then the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured. They honoured Paul's group in many ways and supplied what they needed when they sailed.

After three months they sailed on an Alexandrian ship and came to Italy, landing at Puteoli, where they found believers who invited them to stay a week. And so they came to Rome. The believers there heard they were coming and travelled to meet them. At the sight of these people Paul thanked God and was encouraged.

In Rome, Paul was allowed to live by himself, with a soldier to guard him. He called together the local Jewish leaders and explained that he had done nothing against his people, but was in chains for the hope of Israel. They said they had received no letters about him, but wanted to hear his views, because people everywhere were talking against this sect. On an arranged day, many came. From morning till evening Paul explained God's kingdom and tried to persuade them about Jesus from the Law of Moses and the Prophets. Some were convinced, but others would not believe. Paul quoted Isaiah about people hearing but never understanding, and said, "I want you to know that God's salvation has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen!" (Verse 29 is not in the earliest manuscripts.) For two whole years Paul stayed there in his own rented house and welcomed all who came to see him. He proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness and without hindrance.

summary.bigIdea: Paul reaches Rome at last, and even under guard he keeps proclaiming God's kingdom boldly.
points: On Malta, Paul survives a snakebite and heals many.
Believers come out to meet Paul, and he is encouraged.
For two years in Rome, Paul welcomes everyone and teaches about Jesus "boldly and freely".
summary.reflection: Acts ends with the story still going. How might your life be part of the story that continues?
